capture: Each reduced TU parsed independently in a temporary cwd by the installed original PyJoern; PYTHONPATH removed. No compatibility shim, no mixed-TU Joern run.

knr_const.expected_failure_reason: K&R parameter declarations beginning with const are mistaken for trailing C++ method qualifiers, so a real definition becomes a prototype.
initial_diagnostics: unrecognized top-level brace; possible omitted function definition

global_struct_initializer.expected_failure_reason: A global struct object initializer is mistaken for a record definition and later function bodies are lost.

gnu_inline_asm.expected_failure_reason: GNU inline assembly retains a matching permissive CFG but emits unsupported-expression diagnostics that reject strict DecBench usage.
initial_diagnostics: unsupported expression; CFG parity is unverified

microsoft_asm_block.expected_failure_reason: A Microsoft-style braced inline assembly statement ends method recovery early and prevents recovery of later functions.
initial_diagnostics: unsupported expression; CFG parity is unverified

casted_indirect_call.expected_failure_reason: A dereferenced callee containing nested casts and parentheses is mistaken for an abstract type, creating a missing-expression diagnostic.

terminal_label.expected_failure_reason: Labels immediately before a closing block brace cause missing-expression diagnostics and add incorrect loop edges.

global_qualification.expected_failure_reason: The original frontend accepts leading C++ global qualification in a .c decompiler input; the native prefix parser rejects ::.
initial_diagnostics: unsupported statement; CFG parity is unverified
unsupported expression; CFG parity is unverified
unsupported expression; CFG parity is unverified

missing_goto_target.expected_failure_reason: The original frontend emits a CFG for an unresolved goto in the actual input; the native strict wrapper rejects it. The source really has no corresponding target label.

nested_designator.expected_failure_reason: Chained member initializer designators such as .u.buffers cannot be parsed. The reduced graph matches permissively but strict diagnostics reject it.
initial_diagnostics: unsupported expression; CFG parity is unverified

cpp_operator_declarations.expected_failure_reason: C++ operator prototypes use the original frontend name operator ==, whereas the native parser emits operator== and changes function coverage.

cpp_operator_definitions.expected_failure_reason: C++ operator definitions use the original frontend name ==, whereas the native parser emits operator== and changes function coverage.

noreturn_suffix_unclosed_literal.expected_failure_reason: A definition with an unknown declarator suffix is skipped as a CDT problem declaration; a newline-broken literal leaves a parenthesis unclosed, so the native bracket matcher failed and skipped to the end of the file without a diagnostic.

grouped_pointer_call.expected_failure_reason: A C statement shaped T (*x)(args)... with an unresolved T is a call expression in CDT; the native parser chose a declaration and emptied the enclosing branch.

grouped_pointer_call_typedef.expected_failure_reason: With a typedef binding, CDT keeps T (*x)(args); as a declaration but resolves consecutive parameter lists (a function returning a function) as a call.

call_missing_semicolon_before_loop.expected_failure_reason: An unterminated call followed by another statement, with no later terminator before the closing brace, was claimed whole by terminal-expression recovery, collapsing the method.

literal_callee.expected_failure_reason: A numeric literal called with an empty argument list was a problem statement, removing its label and enclosing branch; CDT parses it as a call.

brace_operand_condition.expected_failure_reason: After a != {0} condition closes its enclosing block, the stray ) problem statement consumed the next statement; CDT ends it after its brace group.
